On a read, `Segment.recordRead(entry, now)` is called (from `Segment.get`/`getLiveValue` lock-free paths) and it does `recencyQueue.add(entry)` — appending to the `recencyQueue` (a `ConcurrentLinkedQueue`-backed `Queue<ReferenceEntry<K,V>>` field) without acquiring the segment lock. That queue is later drained under the lock by `Segment.drainRecencyQueue()` (a `@GuardedBy("this")` method, invoked e.g. during `runLockedCleanup`/post-write-lock processing), which replays the queue entries to reorder the access (LRU) list.

ANSWER: On a read, `LocalCache.Segment.recordRead(entry, now)` is called, which appends the entry to the lock-free `recencyQueue` (`recencyQueue.add(entry)`, guava/src/com/google/common/cache/LocalCache.java:2542-2547) without taking the segment lock; that queue is later drained under the segment lock by `LocalCache.Segment.drainRecencyQueue()` (guava/src/com/google/common/cache/LocalCache.java:2590-2602) to update the actual LRU access-order list.
